## Verdict

missing

## Bearer

ExerciseSessionSystemImpl — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/sensor/session/ExerciseSessionSystemImpl.kt

## Trigger

Each catch block already runs whenever its underlying Health Services
call throws or its registration reports failure — observed.

## Today

Seven sites swallow a failure without writing to the log R79
requires, and one further site drops a returned failure without
reading it (R34):

- `ExerciseSessionSystemImpl.kt:61-63` — `startExerciseSession`'s catch
  around `exerciseClient.startExerciseAsync(...).await()` returns
  `ExerciseSessionStartOutcome.Failed` without logging the caught
  exception.
- `ExerciseSessionSystemImpl.kt:69-71` — `endExerciseSession`'s catch
  around `exerciseClient.endExerciseAsync().await()` returns `false`
  without logging the caught exception.
- `ExerciseSessionSystemImpl.kt:81-83` — `setDataDeliveryMode`'s catch
  around `overrideBatchingModesForActiveExerciseAsync(...).await()`
  returns `false` without logging the caught exception.
- `SensorReadingsSource.kt:77-79` — `unregister`'s catch around
  `measureClient.unregisterMeasureCallbackAsync(...).await()` returns
  `false` without logging the caught exception.
- `SensorReadingsSource.kt:57-65` — `register` returns `false` as soon
  as any `registerOne(dataType)` call fails, without logging which
  data type's registration failed.
- `ExerciseSessionManager.kt:88` (inside `registerReadingsAndStartTicker`,
  called from `open()`) — the `Boolean` `readingsSource.register(...)`
  returns is never read, so a registration failure changes nothing in
  the state `open()` returns.
- `RaceLaunchController.kt:97-103` — `mapOpenResult` maps
  `ExerciseSessionOpenResult.Failed` to `PreparationState.OpenFailed`
  without logging, on the nominal `openPreparation` path (called from
  `confirmConflict` and from the fresh-open branch of
  `openPreparation`), unlike the same file's `reconcileResumedSession`
  (`:75-82`) and `reopenOrphanedSession` (`:90-95`), which log the
  identical outcomes at ERROR under R79.

The system tag carrying the platform's own failure message (e.g.
`SecurityException` naming a missing permission, logged by Health
Services under `WHS_PermissionPolicy`) is never surfaced under this
application's own log tag, so filtering the log on this application
shows nothing when `startExerciseSession` fails.

## Expected

Each of the seven catch or failure sites above writes to
`android.util.Log` at ERROR, naming the operation that failed and the
caught exception or reported failure — never the values R54 forbids
(no heart-rate reading, zone, duration, pace, race name or date; only
the operation and the fault). `ExerciseSessionManager.open()` reads
the `Boolean` `readingsSource.register(...)` returns and acts on a
`false` result rather than discarding it.
